_comment: Atlas Phase 5 outbound Telegram notifier policy. The inbound conversation gateway is native Hermes (operator-configured via `hermes gateway setup`); this file governs ONLY the outbound operational notifier. Credentials are resolved from the env files below in order (first hit wins) so the wizard-written ~/.hermes/.env is reused without duplicating secrets; the alert target chat id is the one value the operator supplies (their numeric Telegram id). Nothing here is committed with real values.

repository_update._comment: Significance policy. Churn is DENY-BY-DEFAULT: only ranges whose changed paths are provably a subset of churn_dirs (and with no recorded spec_version change) are digested instead of paged; any unknown top-level directory escalates to significant. Digested churn is held durably and rides the next significant alert; the backstop flushes it as a standalone digest after digest_backstop_hours. The DISPLAY of a significant alert is governed separately by three OPTIONAL keys (code defaults apply when absent): area_map ({top-level-dir: "core"|"node"|"noise"} for the signal-vs-noise breakdown; any dir absent from the map is surfaced as a new/unclassified area, never hidden), pallet_map ({pallet-name: domain-label} so a pallets/<name> touch is named and interpreted), and light_touch_ratio (0..1, default 0.15; when core-protocol line churn is below this share of total the verdict reads 'large sync, light protocol touch'). These affect wording only, never paging.

chain-runtime-upgrade._comment: Class order is delivery priority: a live chain upgrade surfaces before repo alerts in the same scan.

fleet-signal._comment: Fleet-signals queue (change: fleet-signals): narrative-cluster / watchlist / econ-code instant alerts + durable signal digest lines from the fleet store, read STRICTLY read-only. Priority below chain upgrades, above subtensor repo alerts. digest_backstop_hours flushes pending digest lines as a standalone summary when no instant alert rides them.
